disposition_mapping.rationale: Cycle initiation is unconstrained by design; retained in function but restructured to trigger on an automated calendar and to source assumptions via system feeds rather than manual refresh, reducing FP&A manager effort while preserving the timetable/template issuance function.

Actuals collection is restructured into an automated ingestion pipeline, but the period-cutoff discipline (KB-03) and the need not to distort revenue-recognition-timing assumptions embedded in actuals (KB-13) are preserved through explicit cutoff-rule enforcement and an exception review path for the FP&A analyst.

Driver updates are unconstrained by design and split along the mechanical/judgment line already noted in the baseline: mechanically refreshed drivers (FX, run-rates) move to an automated step, with exchange differences tracked explicitly per KB-08; judgment-based drivers move into the joint assumption-and-submission step with BU finance leads.

BU forecast submission is unconstrained by design and merged with judgment-based driver assumption-setting into one collaborative step, removing a handoff between driver-setting and submission while preserving the commentary and projection outputs.
Consolidation and validation is retained substantially unchanged, continuing to consume closed-period actuals per FPA-R-02, and explicitly applying consistent accounting policy treatment per KB-06.
Variance analysis must survive per FPA-R-01; retained as a distinct step, with automation only assisting bridge generation, not replacing the analytical function.
Management review and approval must survive per FPA-R-03 and must precede publication per FPA-R-04; retained unchanged as the governance gate.
Forecast publication must survive per FPA-R-05 and occurs after TS-07 approval, preserving the FPA-R-04 ordering constraint.

steps.description: Initiate the forecast cycle on an automated rolling-calendar trigger; confirm forecast horizon and granularity; refresh the assumptions pack from system-fed macro indicators and corporate targets; issue timetable and templates to business units via the planning workflow system.
steps.name: Forecast cycle initiation and assumptions refresh

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (exception review) with automated data pipeline
steps.description: Automatically extract closed-period actuals from the GL and management reporting systems via system integration; enforce period cutoff and subledger-lock rules; reconcile completeness and consistency with published results, including consistency of revenue-recognition timing feeding the baseline; load the validated baseline into the forecast model, routing exceptions to an FP&A analyst for review.
steps.name: Automated actuals ingestion and cutoff validation
outputs: closed-period actuals (validated baseline) loaded to forecast model

steps.actor: FP&A analyst with automated driver engine
steps.description: Automatically refresh mechanically determined driver assumptions - FX rates, actual run-rates, indexed cost inflation - via system feeds; track exchange differences explicitly as a distinct log rather than netting them invisibly; flag drivers that instead require business judgment for handling in the joint assumption-setting step.
steps.name: Mechanical driver auto-refresh

steps.actor: BU finance leads (with FP&A analyst facilitation)
steps.description: Business units, facilitated by FP&A, set judgment-based assumptions (pricing, demand, discretionary cost, capex) flagged from the mechanical refresh, and prepare integrated forecast submissions - revenue, cost, headcount, capex - with commentary on changes since the prior forecast, informed by the auto-refreshed mechanical drivers.
steps.name: Judgment-based driver assumptions and BU forecast submissions

steps.description: Consolidate BU submissions into the group forecast model; validate completeness, internal consistency (intercompany, headcount-to-cost coherence), and continuity against closed-period actuals; apply accounting policy treatment consistently across periods; chase and correct anomalous submissions.
steps.name: Consolidation and validation of submissions

steps.description: Analyse the consolidated forecast against budget and against the prior forecast, using automated bridge generation as a starting point; quantify and explain movements by driver and business unit; prepare bridge analyses and risk/opportunity schedules for management review.
steps.name: Variance analysis

steps.description: Present the consolidated forecast and variance analysis to management; conduct challenge sessions on key assumptions; incorporate directed revisions; obtain approval of the forecast as the current planning baseline.
steps.name: Management review and approval

steps.description: Publish the approved forecast: update planning systems and reporting baselines, distribute the forecast pack and commentary to stakeholders, archive the version with its assumptions log.
steps.name: Publish forecast and reporting
